Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)=-\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})=-\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the case $\frac{-\infty }{-\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})} & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{[\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)]^{′}}{[\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{(\frac{1}{x})}{(\frac{3}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{{x}^{-1}}{3{x}^{-1}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
